books.section: Topic 3.12 Movement in the Early Republic

stimulus.text: Paraphrase: After the Revolution, slavery faded in the North, where states passed gradual emancipation laws, and it grew stronger in the South. Eli Whitney’s cotton gin of 1793 made cleaning cotton fast and cheap, so cotton planting spread. The enslaved population of the United States grew from about 500,000 in 1776 to about 700,000 in 1790. At the same time, settlers moving into Kentucky and Tennessee carried enslaved people with them, so slavery spread west with settlement. North of the Ohio River, the Northwest Ordinance of 1787 banned slavery, so the river became a line between free territory to the north and slave states to the south.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase drawn from Barron’s Premium 2027, Chapter 5, Topics 3.7 and 3.12; enslaved-population figures from Barron’s Chapter 5, Topic 3.12.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Barron’s Premium 2027, Chapter 5, Topics 3.7 and 3.12.
stem: Why did slavery grow in Kentucky and Tennessee in the 1790s, even as northern states moved toward emancipation?

options.text: Because the Northwest Ordinance ordered slavery into the new western states.
options.misconception: The Ordinance banned slavery north of the Ohio. Background: Kentucky and Tennessee lie south of it.

options.text: Because Congress passed a law in 1793 requiring western settlers to hold enslaved workers.
options.misconception: Background: no such law existed; settlers chose to bring enslaved workers with them.

options.text: Because northern emancipation laws freed enslaved people and sent them west.
options.misconception: Background: gradual emancipation freed the future children of enslaved mothers in the North; it did not send freed people to Kentucky.

options.text: Because settlers from Virginia and the Carolinas brought enslaved laborers to work their new farms.

rationales.A: The Ordinance banned slavery in its territory; it ordered slavery nowhere.
rationales.B: Background: no law required settlers to hold enslaved workers; they brought them by choice.
rationales.C: Background: northern laws freed children gradually in the North; they sent no one west.
rationales.D: Background: Kentucky and Tennessee were settled largely by people from slaveholding states, who carried enslaved workers with them. Slavery therefore moved west with the settlers.
rationales.general:
1. Background: Kentucky was settled from Virginia, and Tennessee from North Carolina.
2. Background: both were slaveholding states.
3. Settlers carried their labor system with them when they moved.
4. So slavery spread west because people carried it, not because a law ordered it there.
Remember: when people move, they carry their way of life with them — ask where the settlers came from.
